name: nlp_keras_text_bad
title: A Keras BiLSTM review classifier whose holdout is cut from a reshuffling tf.data pipeline, whose vocabulary is adapted on every review, and whose sigmoid head is paired with from_logits=True
origin: hardening round 2, domain-nlp, 2026-09-14 - the defective twin of nlp_keras_text
note: MLView reports NOTHING on this program today - six planted defects, four of them modelled by a rule, two of those high severity, and the document carries zero findings in both dataflow modes. Three separate holes produce that silence and each has its own minimal repro: MLV121 cannot follow a tf.data.Dataset that reaches the splitting helper through a factory (NLP2-04); MLV709 does not fire when build_model() and compile_model(model) are BOTH used, although each hop works alone (NLP2-06); and MLV601 goes quiet for the same reason, because model.fit's receiver never resolves (NLP2-01). The deliver stage is also declared absent even though model.save is called on line 56.

expected.defect: the holdout is cut with take/skip out of a shuffle that has no reshuffle_each_iteration=False
expected.why: tf.data redraws the buffer on every epoch, so the rows in `test` change every pass: the holdout does not exist, and the reported test accuracy is a training accuracy

expected.defect: the output layer applies a sigmoid and the loss is BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True)
expected.why: the loss squashes the already-squashed output a second time, so the gradients saturate and the model settles on a confident-looking constant

expected.defect: the correct twin's keras.utils.set_random_seed / enable_op_determinism pair has been deleted
expected.why: with an unseeded tf.data shuffle deciding the split (see MLV121) two runs of this script do not even train on the same rows

expected.defect: sklearn's accuracy_score is handed model.predict probabilities instead of (probabilities > 0.5)
expected.why: accuracy_score compares floats against 0/1 labels, so the printed test accuracy is 0.0 whatever the model does

forbidden.why: compile_model() calls model.compile(...) on line 33 - the defect here is what it compiles with, not that it does not compile
MLV301 is a torch rule; this workspace has no torch at all and keras.Model has no .eval()
the same - torch.no_grad() does not exist in TensorFlow
no torch DataLoader exists in this project
the same, and main() sits behind the __main__ guard (line 60)
no .cuda() and no torch.device literal appears anywhere in this project
no nn.Module subclass is defined anywhere in this project
the model is written with keras' own model.save (line 56); torch.save and torch.load do not appear
there is no Lightning code here
there is no HuggingFace Trainer here
MLV601 is a whole-workspace claim and is labelled once, on train_text.py; a second finding in vectorize.py would be a duplicate of one root cause

unsupported.defect: the TextVectorization vocabulary and its 20 000-token ranking are adapted on every review in the file, including the ones the take/skip holdout will keep back
unsupported.why: keras.layers.TextVectorization.adapt has no FIT / FIT_TRANSFORM role in MLView's knowledge tables, so MLV101 cannot see the Keras spelling of fit_transform-before-split at all

unsupported.defect: train_ds and val_ds are drawn from the same reshuffling pipeline, so the validation loss printed each epoch is computed on rows the model trained on in an earlier epoch
unsupported.why: MLV107 is a later-tier rule and is not built; MLV121 covers the shuffle half of the same defect

unsupported.defect: the correct twin's EarlyStopping / ModelCheckpoint pair is gone, so the saved model is simply the last epoch's
unsupported.why: MLV802 is a later-tier rule and is not built
